Integrating radial gamma densities gives lambda_0=1-e^-t(1+t), lambda_n=G_n(t)+e^-t*t^n(n-1-t)/n!, the exact adjacent gap -e^-t*t^n*(t-n)*(t-n-1)/(n+1)!, and lambda_1-lambda_0=e^-t*t(1-t). For t<1 all higher modes decrease from mode1; for 1<t<2 mode0 dominates mode1 and mode2 by explicit positive differences; for t>=2 the only positive-index competitor is either mode1 or a larger-index local maximum. The strict gamma-density pairing integral proves lambda_(m+1)(m+1)<1/2, while lambda_0(2)>1/2, eliminating the competitor. Compactness follows from t^n/n! control for fixed t. At t=1 exactly modes 0,1,2 tie; branch differentiation gives the claimed one-sided cusp. Independent mpmath integration/gap checks across 207 cases support the algebra but are not the quantified proof.
